  HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee
  Regular Meeting of March 4, 2025
  CITY HALL • 111 S. FIRST ST.

  Committee Chair Vallejos called the meeting to order at 6:33 pm.

2. Approval of Minutes: 9/5/2023; 5/7/2024; 9/3/2024; 12/3/2024; 2/4/2025

  Staff Liaison Alvarez informed the Committee that no meetings were held on 9/3/2024 and
  2/4/2025 due to a lack of quorum. However, since these meetings were noticed and posted
  online for the public, staff wanted to officially state for the record that the meetings did not
  occur, despite being posted and noticed to the community.

  Motion: Motion to approve minutes by Committee member Soto, and seconded by
  Tousignant. All present committee members approved; motion passed.

3. PROGRESS REPORTS

  Management Analyst Esteban Alvarez presented the Committee with most up to date
  progress reports for FY 2024-2025 for the Senior Case Management, Code Enforcement,
  Housing Rights Center, and Home Improvement Programs. Staff requested that the reports be
  received and filed by the committee.

  Committee Action:

  Vice Chair McCammon presented supplemental documents to the Committee regarding the
  Housing Rights Center and expressed concerns about the agency’s staffing levels and phone
  response times. Committee member Cardenas suggested exploring other agencies and
  resources to complement the Housing Rights Center’s services. Consultant Tam noted that
  additional resources for the community, as per her previous recommendations, are available
  and listed on the City of Alhambra's website.
  Page 1 of 3
  Motion: The Committee received and filed the informational reports.

4. WORKING MEETING IN PREPERATION OF THE 2025-2029 CONSOLIDATED
  PLAN AND 2025-26 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN.

  Consultant Veronica Tam presented to the HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee on the
  Consolidated Plan and Analysis of Impediments to Fair Housing, covering the CDBG and
  HOME programs. The presentation included an overview of the goals of these programs, a
  map showing low and moderate-income areas, potential uses for the funds, beneficiaries,
  current goals and priorities, program limitations, eligible public services and expenditure
  caps, as well as eligible activities and improvements. Consultant Tam also referenced the
  updated Low/Moderate Income Map and outlined the upcoming timeline, which includes
  presenting a draft to the Committee in April and a 30-day Public Review Period to follow.

  Committee member Renee-Marie inquired if CDBG funds could be used for a Dog Park.
  Staff responded that a Dog Park is already in development, with an expected opening date in
  Summer 2025.

  Vice-Chair McCammon asked if CDBG funds could be used for street lights. Consultant
  Tam stated that yes, CDBG can be used to improve street lights. Vice Chair McCammon
  also inquired with Code Enforcement Supervisor Perez-Garcia about whether the Fire
  Department conducts rental inspections. Supervisor Perez-Garcia responded that he was
  unaware of any such inspections being conducted by the Fire Department. However, he did
  mention that his department collaborates closely with the Housing Rights Center, receiving
  referrals from them and providing referrals in return.

  Public Comment: Shirley Tatsuno inquired about the possibility of allocating $20,000 from
  CDBG funds to support Family Promise of San Gabriel Valley, an organization that assists
  families experiencing or at risk of homelessness. Mrs. Tatsuno also mentioned Habitat for
  Humanity and expressed hope that the organization could collaborate with the City.

5. STAFF UPDATES

 Staff provided the HCDA with an update on the current funding status of the CDBG and
 HOME programs. Staff reached out to the local representative from the Los Angeles branch
 of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), who advised that the
 Consolidated Plans and Action Plans should proceed as usual. No changes in funding
 availability were reported at this time.

6. COMMENTS FROM THE AUDIENCE

  Lahiru Kodituwakku from the Community Health Alliance addressed the audience regarding
  smoke-free housing in multi-unit buildings in the City of Alhambra. According to Lahiru,
  Alhambra currently holds a C rating for secondhand smoke exposure, with one-third of the
  City's residents being affected by secondhand smoke.

    SUBSTANTIAL AMENDMENT
  to the
  CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  2025-2029 CONSOLIDATED PLAN and
  2025-2026 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN

SUMMARY

The City of Alhambra is a federal entitlement community that receives an annual
allocation of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) and HOME funds from the
US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). As an entitlement
community, the City is required to prepare an Annual Action Plan detailing the City’s uses
and priorities of CDBG and HOME funds to meets its affordable housing and community
development goals as outlined in the Consolidated Plan. For Program Year 2025-2026,
the City is proposing a Substantial Amendment to the Action Plan and the 2025-2029
Consolidated Plan to include a $4,079,000 Section 108 Loan Guarantee under CDBG to
fund the project management for the development of the Alhambra Community Center.
This effort is in alignment with the City’s goals as stated in the 2025-2029 Consolidated
Plan to provide public facilities improvements.

In accordance with Federal Regulations, the City is required to notify and provide citizens
with an opportunity to comment on all proposed Substantial Amendments to the City’s
Consolidated Plan and Annual Action Plan. The City will accept comments on the
proposed Substantial Amendment to the 2025-26 Action Plan and the 2025-2029
Consolidated Plan for a period of 30 days from September 12, 2025 through October 13,
2025.

PROPOSED CHANGES

The City of Alhambra is an Entitlement Grantee under the Community Development Block
Grant (CDBG) Program, which funds are administered by the U.S. Department of Housing
and Urban Development (HUD). From time to time, it is necessary for the City to process
Substantial Amendments to the Consolidated Plan and the Annual Action Plan to allow
for new CDBG or HOME funded activities; modification of existing activities; or other
program administrative actions.

The City is seeking to establish a new public facility activity under the 2025-2026 Action
Plan from the application and use of Section 108 Loan Guarantee funds under CDBG.
The project is an eligible CDBG activity under the provisions of 24 CFR 570.702 for the
Eligible Entity for Section 108; Section 570.703(l) for Public Facilities as an Eligible
Activity; and Section 570.201 of the federal regulations for Public Facility Improvements,
and it meets the National Objective of benefiting Low and Moderate-Income Areas
570.208(a)(1)(i) and 570.483(b)(1)(i).
 This proposal requires a Substantial Amendment to the City’s 2025-2029 Consolidated
Plan and 2025-2026 Action Plan to include a funding mechanism and an activity not
previously identified. The activity is established pursuant to authorizing the submittal of
a Section 108 Loan Guarantee Application. As part of the Section 108 Loan, the City will
amend the current year’s CDBG Program Action Plan to include the Alhambra Community
Center Project and the use of Section 108 funds. Similarly, the 2025-2029 Consolidated
Plan will be amended to include the use of Section 108 Loan Guarantee funds to manage
the development of the community center.

The City of Alhambra will allocate $4,079,000 of CDBG Section 108 Loan funding for
Program Year 2025-2026 for project management of the Alhambra Community Center at
a 1.38 acre parcel at 612 West Shorb Street. The Community Center will include but is
not limited to classrooms, multi-purpose rooms, meeting rooms, fitness areas, lobby,
storage, administration offices, recreation rooms, courtyard, and parking facilities. The
Community Center Project is estimated at $30,900,000; the remainder of the Project costs
will be funded by $25,000,000 from the California State Budget and $1,821,000 from the
City’s General Fund. The CDBG Section 108 Loan will provide the gap financing
necessary to complete the project.

2025-2029 CONSOLIDATED PLAN AMENDMENT

The following sections of the 2020-2024 Consolidated Plan will be amended:

A. Strategic Plan – SP-25 Priority Needs – 91.215(a)(2)

Priority Need #6 (Page 72): Add in the description section the use of Section 108 Loan
Guarantee funds for public improvements; specifically, for the development of a new
community center at 612 West Shorb Street, Alhambra, CA. The City is proposing to
utilize $4,079,000 (five times the City’s CDBG allocation) for project management of the
Alhambra Community Center. Consistent with CDBG National Objectives, the project
shall benefit the low and moderate-income area as specified under 570.208(a)(1)(i) and
570.483(b)(1)(i) of the Federal Regulations. The repayment of the loan shall be over
twenty years with the first-year payment expected in 2026-27. Completion of the
Alhambra Community Center Project is anticipated by May 2027.

INTRODUCTION

As a recipient of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funding, the City of Alhambra is
eligible to participate in the Section 108 Loan Guarantee program administered by the US
Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). Under this program, the City can
leverage up to five times its annual CDBG allocation for large community development
investments.

Under Alhambra’s 2025-2026 Action Plan and 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan, the City identified
providing community facilities and infrastructure and providing community and supportive
services as high need. In addition, the City’s Strategic Plan and Community Survey also identified
these priorities as high need, suggesting public spaces and related programming are essential to

  D
quality of life, recreation and communing in Alhambra.

To support the community’s interests, the City is proposing to utilize $4,079,000 in CDBG funds

  R
to enable the development of the Alhambra Community Center located at 612 West Shorb Street
in Alhambra, CA.

The Alhambra Community Center involves partial preservation/ adaptive reuse (8,855 square

  T
feet) of the former Shorb Medical Facility and the addition of 8,239 square feet or more of new

  AF
facility space for active recreation and enrichment programming including classes, meeting
rooms, special events, social interaction, health and wellness, educational programs, youth and
senior activities, technology access, and specialized services which collectively serve as a central
hub of resources and support services for Alhambra’s diverse age groups and backgrounds.
Facility features include classrooms, multi-purpose rooms, meeting rooms, fitness areas, lobby,
storage, administration offices, recreation rooms, courtyard, and parking facilities. Alhambra
does not currently have a community center despite a population of 83,000 people; therefore,
the development of this facility not only provides opportunity to enhance civic engagement and
cultural exchange, but also strengthens social bonds and contributes to a more vibrant
community.

In 2023, the City of Alhambra was awarded $25,000,000 from the State of California under the
2023 Budget Act for the construction of the Alhambra Community Center; however, due to price
escalation, additional funds are necessary to ensure the completion of this important public
improvement project. The Section 108 Loan Guarantee Program under CDBG provides the City
of Alhambra with the low-cost, long-term financing it needs.

LOCATION AND PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The existing site for the Alhambra Community Center (on 1.38 acres) was formerly the Shorb
Medical Clinic, located at 612 West Shorb Street. The facility has been vacant for approximately
seventeen years and previously operated as a medical clinic by Los Angeles County. The City

  2
 resumed ownership of the property in 2019. The facility is closed, blighted, unattractive, and
unsafe. It has often been vandalized; police have found squatters. The building is also structurally
and seismically unstable and has fallen into significant disrepair. Overall, the interior and exterior
are in shambles with lead and asbestos throughout.

Once revitalized, the Alhambra Community Center will be the center of the community providing
recreational and educational programming for all. It will immediately attract community interest
and enable resources to be efficiently and effectively allocated toward options the residents need
and desire most including passive and active uses with an appropriate nexus to Moor Sports Field
and the surrounding neighborhood.

The City expects to complete the Alhambra Community Center Project by May 2027.

The cost of the Alhambra Community Center is based on several factors including the design plan,

  R

Section 108 loan proceeds form a key component of the financing for this project. The City is

the 2025-26 Program Year, less any outstanding Section 108 Loan balances (Alhambra has no

funds in any given year. In the event the United States Congress terminates the CDBG program

570.704 del Código de Regulaciones Federales. El Proyecto propuesto para su financiación es el siguiente:
PRIMERA ENMIENDA AL PLAN DE ACCIÓN ANUAL 2025-2026 Y AL PLAN CONSOLIDADO
2025-2029 PARA LA CREACIÓN DE UN PROYECTO DE INSTALACIONES PÚBLICAS (CENTRO
COMUNITARIO ALHAMBRA)
La Ciudad está buscando enmendar el Plan de Acción Anual 2025-2026 y el Plan Consolidado 2025-2029
para crear un Proyecto de Instalaciones Públicas (Centro Comunitario Alhambra) para permitir la construcción
de un nuevo centro comunitario de 17,000 pies cuadrados, ubicado en a 612 West Shorb Street, Alhambra,
California (anteriormente Centro Médico Shorb), para brindar programas recreativos y de enriquecimiento
a los miembros de la comunidad en apoyo a las necesidades de alta prioridad. La Ciudad pretende utilizar
hasta $4,079,000 en fondos del Préstamo de la Sección 108 de HUD como financiación complementaria para
completar la implementación del Proyecto de Instalaciones Públicas. El uso que la Ciudad haga de los fondos
del Préstamo de la Sección 108 deberán ser reembolsados en un plazo de veinte (20) años. Como parte del
procesamiento del Préstamo de la Sección 108, la Ciudad necesita enmendar el Plan de Acción Anual y el
Plan Consolidado actual para incluir el Proyecto del Centro Comunitario Alhambra y el uso de los fondos del
Préstamo de la Sección 108.
El Proyecto es elegible para el uso del financiamiento del Préstamo de la Sección 108, según lo dispuesto
por CFR 570.703(l) y 570.201(c). La construcción de las nuevas instalaciones del centro comunitario cumplirá
con los Objetivos Nacionales de actividades que beneficien a un área de ingresos bajos y moderados (LMA,
por sus siglas en inglés) — Sección 570.483(b)(1)(i). Para que el Proyecto propuesto sea elegible para recibir
asistencia, al menos el 51% de los residentes en el área son personas de ingresos bajos y moderados.
PRESENTACIÓN DE UNA SOLICITUD DE PRÉSTAMO DE LA SECCIÓN 108
La Ciudad está solicitando la aprobación para presentar una solicitud de Préstamo de la Sección 108 por
$4,079,000 a HUD para implementar el Proyecto de Instalaciones Públicas (Centro Comunitario Alhambra).
Con frecuencia, las ciudades desean apoyar actividades elegibles para el CDBG; sin embargo, el tamaño y
el alcance de los proyectos superan el monto anual asignado por el CDBG. En lugar de tener que acumular
suficientes fondos de CDBG a lo largo de varios años, la Ley de Vivienda y Desarrollo Comunitario de 1974
creó el Programa de Préstamos de la Sección 108. Las ciudades pueden pedir prestado hasta cinco veces
su asignación anual de CDBG y devolver el préstamo en un plazo de hasta 20 años, a tasas de interés muy
competitivas.
La Ciudad es elegible para recibir asistencia de la garantía de préstamo, según lo detallado en el Título 24
de CFR 570.702(a). El préstamo ayudará a financiar la construcción del Centro Comunitario Alhambra, según
lo dispuesto por CFR 570.703(l). El Proyecto también está siendo financiado por fondos de subvención
otorgados por la suma de $25 millones del Estado de California (Ley de Presupuesto 2023) para construir un
nuevo centro comunitario en 612 Shorb Street.
